title: Higher-Order Continuation Correctness

basis.scope: Establish bounded correctness conditions for higher-order continuation semantics, including HC(C), T(C), and Lift(C), without asserting universal higher-order correctness.

core_rule.statement: Higher-order continuation correctness applies only after EVAL_024 and only to explicit higher-order continuations that satisfy higher-order admissibility; Lift(C) preserves continuation identity and process-equivalence class where defined; T(C) preserves typing, admissibility, and process equivalence where defined; bounded strategy correctness remains governing; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Establish bounded correctness conditions for higher-order continuation semantics, including HC(C), T(C), and Lift(C), without asserting universal higher-order correctness.

canonical_claims.statement: Higher-order correctness is bounded and applies only to explicit higher-order continuation classes.
Lift(C) preserves continuation identity and process-equivalence class where defined.
T(C) preserves typing, admissibility, and process equivalence where defined.
Higher-order reduction remains subject to EVAL_024, REDUCE_025, and bounded strategy correctness.

formal_objects.name: Higher-Order Continuation Correctness
formal_objects.definition: The bounded property that higher-order continuation operations preserve typing, process equivalence, admissibility, strategy correctness, and canonical outcomes.

formal_objects.name: Lift Correctness
formal_objects.definition: The property that Lift(C) embeds a first-order continuation into the higher-order domain without changing its continuation identity or process equivalence class.

formal_objects.name: Transformation Correctness
formal_objects.definition: The property that a lawful continuation transformation T(C) preserves typing, admissibility, and process equivalence where defined.

formal_objects.name: Higher-Order Correctness Class
formal_objects.definition: The class of higher-order continuations satisfying all bounded higher-order correctness prerequisites.

then: Higher-order transformation preserves process equivalence where defined.
Canonical outcomes remain NF(C), pNF(C), or ⊥C_x.

correctness_obligations.description: Lift(C) embeds first-order continuations without altering identity, type, or process-equivalence class.
T(C) preserves typing, admissibility, and process equivalence where defined.
Higher-order continuation operands remain lawful continuation objects.
S(C) remains applicable to higher-order reduction candidates.
Higher-order reduction outcomes remain within NF(C), pNF(C), or classified ⊥C_x.

limitations: Applies only to bounded higher-order continuation classes.
Does not prove universal higher-order correctness.
Does not permit self-modifying calculus rules.
invariants: Higher-order correctness does not introduce new primitives.
Higher-order operations remain subject to EVAL_024 and REDUCE_025.
Strategy correctness from PATCH_PI_RT_CALCULUS_036 remains governing.

Lift(C) and lawful transformations preserve typing and process equivalence where defined.
